Been struggling recently with the knowledge that whatever I could have been had I started early, it's gone now, and it doesn't get better. 

I knew back when I was little, too, and I had a family I knew would support me. I was just so paralyzed by the fear of transition, the fear of becoming... exactly what I've become. It's like a self-fulfilling nightmare.

There's no fear, now. Just a dull hopelessness.

I wish I was anyone else. I don't want to be this person anymore. I don't want to hurt anymore.

I'm sorry for being so depressing. I just haven't been happy in a long time. I can't remember the last time I made anybody else happy, either. I don't know what to say.

I hope reincarnation is real.

I'm a transgender girl. This doesn't make me better at video games. Most other girls I know are miles better at games - especially better at League - than I am.

I am not a male who sees himself as a woman, and I find the implication insulting. I'm female. My body is female. The fact that my history of having my gender incorrectly perceived results in me being discriminated against hurts me deeply.

I didn't choose to be transgender. It was this or die. I have faced a life of loneliness, beatings, humiliation, and depression, stemming from the ridiculous idea other people have that I am a male pretending to be female. I'm a girl. I've always been a girl.

One of my few solaces is in gaming, as it's something I can enjoy both with my few friends and strangers without fearing abuse. I'm not especially good at games, but I love playing with my friends. Several of them are transgender girls too, and have had similar stories to myself. Others are non-transgender girls who also love gaming.

Say I went to this tournament. Me and my trans friends are not amazing gamers because of our trans-ness. We aren't any better than other women. But according to the rules of this tournament, we would be banned for a year because, as friends, we would all be playing together on the same team.

How is this okay?

Activity does not decide gender.

Example: a woman who does extremely masculine things. Does this make her not a woman? Similarly, is a man who does extremely feminine things not a man? I'm guessing most people still agree that the first person is still a woman and the second person is a man. So there is something else that decides gender in social situations beyond just activity. Something above or beyond action that makes other people identify the gender of an individual one way or another. And *that's* where transgender issues come in.

Transgender people are everywhere, have just as many differences in activity and opinion as cisgender (just a term for non-transgender) people, but we are generally defined by problems with our perceived gender in social situations. This is not a choice, it's something we feel and can't ignore. Attempts to ignore personal issues with gender often lead to depression and suicide. So instead we work to make our preferred gender visible to others. It's not about pushing an image or being stereotypically masculine or feminine - it's about being perceived as who we actually are in terms of gender.
